gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Bevellier cuts its lowercase tall and wide from flat, single-weight strokes, with every glyph packed tight against its neighbours. And Noto Sans Sundanese sits beneath it as a sans with open crossbars on the e, loosening the tension the heading builds.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Graceful, and a bit like bent wire, Bevellier draws its letters in one unbroken line. Noto Sans Sunuwar follows in a plain sans with curves that leave daylight inside them, and its short ascender stems keep the text looking low and settled under that tight display lettering.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nag: Sophisticated and flat, Bevellier holds every stroke to the thickness of a drawn wire, with tightly packed letters and squat ascenders. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri brings short ascenders and a tall x-height beneath it.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Noto Sans Syriac has tall lowercase bowls like blown glass bulbs. Under Bevellier's tightly spaced, wire-constant strokes, those rounded forms and easy s turns give the page a looser texture to move through.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-syriac-eas: Noto Sans Syriac Eastern keeps its tall lowercase standing against small caps, with curve endings that never crowd one another. Bevellier above it has crossbars as heavy as its stems, so the page moves from dense to open.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-syriac-wes: Graceful, stencil-flat Bevellier is built from rounded rods of a single weight. It does its best work as display lettering, while Noto Sans Syriac Western, a modern sans-serif with terminals held far from the stroke, handles the quieter running text.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Sophisticated and tightly spaced, Bevellier draws its bowls and stems at the same weight. Noto Sans Tagalog then fills the line with a dominant middle zone and generous gaps in its curves, a plain sans that lets the heading's density stand out.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Uppercase letters built from lines of one constant thickness give Bevellier a flat, stencil-cut look, with a tall, wide lowercase. And Noto Sans Tagbanwa answers in open, clear-gapped sans-serif curves that fill most of the line's height.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Noto Sans Tai Le tapers its ink strokes out before they touch and keeps the step from capitals to lowercase minimal. Bevellier's plain, unshaded line never swells.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Professional in manner, Bevellier holds the steady line of a technical drafting pen, with squat ascenders and tight spacing. Noto Sans Tai Viet takes over with short ascenders and a tall x-height, while Bevellier earns its keep big and brief.
